findings.description: The HEAD authoritative package_scope check still fails closed only on string glob match. validate_package_scope delegates to validate_scope_compliance, which fnmatches each files_modified entry without normalizing '.'/'..'. A schema-valid repo-relative path such as 'src/api/../../SECRET.md' matches package_def write_allow 'src/api/**' (fnmatch treats the literal prefix as a match) even though the logical path is outside that tree. FilePath only forbids a leading slash, so the payload stays schema-valid. End-to-end reproduction: accept_package_result accepted a result with files_modified=['src/api/../../SECRET.md'], worker-echoed scope.write_allow=['**'], and package_def.scope.write_allow=['src/api/**'] once the commit check passed. That bypasses the security intent of checking package_def scope instead of the worker echo.
findings.resolution: Normalize each files_modified path inside validate_scope_compliance before allow/deny matching (collapse '.'/'..', reject empty paths and paths that escape the repo root, reject absolute paths). Match only the normalized relative path. Optionally tighten work-queue FilePath to disallow '..' segments. Add an accept_package_result / validate_package_scope regression for 'src/api/../../outside.py' against write_allow ['src/api/**'].

findings.description: HEAD covers broadened echoed scope, package deny, missing package scope.write_allow, and a nameless failing step, but does not pin path-traversal files_modified against package_scope or accept_package_result. The authoritative scope refusal can therefore regress without a red test.
findings.resolution: Add tests in test_result_validator.py and test_validate_work_result.py asserting that files_modified entries containing '..' are refused when package_def.scope.write_allow is a directory glob such as 'src/api/**'.
